# Extracting the secret

minapp holds a secret: `SecretVault.getSecret()` returns
`rzfrida{f1nd_th3_s3cr3t}`. The app never displays it: the method is called
internally, as part of the license checks, and the result is hidden inside
the app. We still want to see it.

## 1. Understand where the secret flows

Open the app and press Activate License with a wrong key. The feedback line
reads `Invalid license key`. The app's activation logic compared the key
against the license constant *and* against the secret (twice: once in Java,
once in native code): and told us none of them matched.

The secret itself never shows up on screen.

## 2. Hook getSecret

Attach and load the example hook `docs/examples/hooks/extract_secret.js`:

```js
Java.perform(function () {
  var Vault = Java.use('re.frida.minapp.secret.SecretVault');
  Vault.getSecret.implementation = function () {
    var real = this.getSecret();
    console.log('getSecret() -> ' + real);
    return real;
  };
  Vault.checkSecret.implementation = function (input) {
    var real = this.checkSecret(input);
    console.log('checkSecret("' + input + '") -> ' + real);
    return real;
  };
  console.log('SecretVault hooks installed');
});
```

Inside the override, `this.getSecret()` calls the *original* method: frida
keeps it reachable. The wrapper only logs and forwards.

```text
[0x00000000]> Froj frida://attach/usb//FridaMin
{"ok":true,"result":{"action":"attach","pid":3718,"resumed":false,"state":"attached"}}

[0x00000000]> Frlj docs/examples/hooks/extract_secret.js
{"ok":true,"result":{"value":null,"type":"undefined"}}
```

## 3. Trigger the check

Type anything into the license field and press Activate License. The
activation path calls `SecretVault.checkSecret`, which calls `getSecret`,
and our hook records it. Drain the agent output:

```text
[0x00000000]> Frmj
{"ok":true,"result":{"messages":[{"kind":"send","payload":{"type":"agent.ready","version":1}},{"kind":"log","level":"info","text":"SecretVault hooks installed"},{"kind":"log","level":"info","text":"getSecret() -> rzfrida{f1nd_th3_s3cr3t}"},{"kind":"log","level":"info","text":"checkSecret(\"notthekey\") -> false"}],"dropped":0}}
```

`getSecret() -> rzfrida{f1nd_th3_s3cr3t}`. The hook captured the secret on
its way through the app's own code.

![The hook reveals the secret](img/android_journey/secret-hooked.png)

> **Note:** `console.log` inside the agent arrives as `{"kind":"log",...}`
> messages, drained by `Frmj`. The `agent.ready` event is the agent
> booting. Later drains only carry new messages.

## 4. Confirm it with the app itself

Type the captured secret into the license field and press Activate License.
The feedback line now reads `Secret verified`: the app agrees that we know
the secret.

## 5. The secret also lives in native memory

The C side of the app holds the same secret: `libnative.so` decodes it into
a global `g_secret` at load time. Find it by scanning the module for the
full byte pattern:

```js
var m = Process.enumerateModules().filter(function (x) { return x.name === 'libnative.so'; })[0];
var hits = Memory.scanSync(m.base, m.size, '72 7a 66 72 69 64 61 7b 66 31 6e 64 5f 74 68 33 5f 73 33 63 72 33 74 7d');
console.log('full-secret hits: ' + hits.map(function (h) { return h.address.toString(); }).join(', '));
```

```text
[0x00000000]> Frlj docs/examples/hooks/scan_secret.js
[0x00000000]> Frmj
... "text":"full-secret hits: 0x7adfac856690"
```

Exactly one hit. Read it with `Frxj`:

```text
[0x00000000]> Frxj 0x7adfac856690 24
{"ok":true,"result":{"address":"0x7adfac856690","size":24,"bytes":"727a66726964617b66316e645f7468335f7333637233747d"}}
```

To include the C string's terminating NUL, read 25 bytes instead. The reply
then ends in `00`.

![The secret in native memory](img/android_journey/secret-native.png)

The hex decodes to `rzfrida{f1nd_th3_s3cr3t}`: the same secret, in the
memory of `libnative.so`.

> **Note:** scan for the *full* pattern. The compiler folds the XOR decode
> at `-O2`, so fragments of the plaintext exist in the module's read-only
> data. A short prefix pattern matches those fragments too, and only the
> full pattern pinpoints the live `g_secret`.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Try

Hook `getSecret`, press Activate License with any input, drain `Frmj`,
then scan `libnative.so` for the full pattern and read the hit with
`Frxj`.
:::
